contexts.text: The Last Judgment was executed... lastly upon the Reformed.
In the middle appeared those called the Reformed, distinct according to their countries. Enumerated. LJCont 20.
Priests from the Reformed were sent to instruct the good Papists.
The Last Judgment upon the Reformed, who are called also Protestants and Evangelicals. Described. LJCont 14, General article. SE 5202. SE 5347. SE 5937. SE 5948.
The reason the Reformed constituted the Middle, was that by them the Word is read, and the Lord is worshipped, and hence the greatest light is with them... AR 631:2.
Upon whom from the Reformed the Last Judgment was executed. General article.

After the Reformation, as they began to make a distinction between charity and faith, and to worship God under three Persons... these heavenly truths were hidden from them; (for otherwise) they would have falsified them...
By the kings of the earth are meant the Reformed, who are in falsities of doctrine.

(Thus) the Word which is in the Church of the Reformed, illustrates all nations and peoples by a spiritual communication... Therefore, when the Word had been almost rejected by the Papists, of the Divine Providence the Reformation took place, and thence the Word was again received... Inv 24.
A blind faith continued afterwards with many of the Reformed, for the reason that they had separated faith from charity. Explained.
(The Reformed who are in faith alone, and those not in faith alone.) DFaith 42, Described. DFaith 43, Described.
He replied, I am a Reformed Christian. DFaith 43. TCR 391.
Afterwards, when the Church was Reformed, and faith alone was received... the Lord's Human could be regarded no otherwise (than as that of any other man).
Preface. The Doctrinals of the Church and Religion of the Reformed. (Quoted at full length.)
In the middle of the gathering were the Reformed, and many of the clergy. (They could not say One God, nor Divine Human.)
Preface. () treats of the Church of the Reformed, the quality of those there who are in faith alone...

The Church in the Reformed world is at this day divided into three, from its three leaders, Luther, Calvin, and Melancthon; and these three Churches disagree in various things, but all agree in this article: that man is justified by faith without the works of the law; which is a marvellous thing.

Preface. On the exploration and manifestation of the state of life of those in the Church of the Reformed who are called learned and wise from the confirmation of faith separated from charity, and of justification and Salvation through this faith. Treated of. AR 421.

The exploration and manifestation of the state of life with those in the Church of the Reformed, who are not so wise, yet place the all of religion in faith... and thus live at their pleasure. Signified, Explained.

Those in the Church of the Reformed who are not so spiritually dead from visionary reasonings, the love of self, the conceit of Own intelligence, and the concupiscences thence, as the former, and still have made faith alone the head of their religion. Signified, Explained.

Preface. On the exploration and manifestation of those in the Churches of the Reformed; here, who believe in the Lord, that He is the God of Heaven and earth... and that His Human is Divine; and that this has not been received there, and can with difficulty be received, so long as the dogma of justification by faith alone is seated in their hearts. Treated of.
Preface. Further, on the state of the Church with the Reformed, the quality of those who are interiorly in faith alone against the two essentials of the New Church... Treated of.

Contrary to the two essentials received in the Church of the Reformed: a Trinity of Persons, and that faith alone saves without the works of the law; and that from this contrariety, the two essentials of the New Church... are a matter of contempt, trouble, and aversion. Signified, Explained.
(The aversion of the Reformed for actual repentance. Explained.)
A great red dragon = those in the Church of the Reformed, who make God three, and the Lord two, and who separate faith from charity, and make the former (alone) saving. Explained.

The dragon is called great because all of the Church of the Reformed distinguish God into Three Persons, and make faith solely saving, except some here and there who do not believe in like manner concerning the Trinity and faith.
The beast out of the sea = the laity in the Churches of the Reformed who are in the doctrine and faith of the dragon... Explained.
That all of the Church of the Reformed have acknowledged... this heresy... except those who have believed in the Lord. Sig and Explained.
The beast out of the earth = the clergy of the Churches of the Reformed who are in the doctrine and faith of the dragon. Explained.
Three hundred of the clergy of the Reformed world, all learned... ascended into an angelic Society... they were seen as calves... and, when they cast themselves down, as dead horses. Explained.
Preface. In () the evils and falsities in the Church of the Reformed are disclosed by influx from Heaven. Treated of.

Influx from the Lord out of the inmost Heaven into the Church of the Reformed where are those in faith separated from charity as to doctrine and as to life, to take away from them truths and goods, and to open the falsities and evils in which they are; and thus to separate them from those who believe in the Lord, and, from Him, are in charity and its faith. Signified, Explained.
Into those who are in the interiors of the Church of the Reformed, and who study the doctrine of justification by faith alone, who are called the clergy. Signified, Explained.
The influx of truth and good from the Lord with those in the Church of the Reformed who are in its externals, and in that faith, and who are called the laity. Signified, Explained.
The influx from the Lord into all things together with the men of the Church of the Reformed. Signified, Explained.
That the Roman Catholic religiosity as to doctrine reigns... also in some part even yet with the Reformed. Signified, Explained.
If the papal dominion had not been broken at the time of the Reformation...
That all, from various heresies among the Reformed, who had not lived according to the Lord's precepts... being judged from the Word, perish. Signified, Explained.
The reason it treats here concerning combat with the Reformed... is that the Reformed read the Word, and acknowledge the truths there as Divine.
This dogma (that the understanding must see nothing in theological matters) the Church of the Reformed has retained from the Roman Catholic religiosity.

That the Churches separated by the Reformation from the Roman Catholic Church disagree in various things; but all agree in the articles concerning the Trinity of Persons, the origin of sin from Adam, the imputation of the merit of Christ, and justification by faith alone. General article.
The Evangelicals and the Reformed are together called Protestants. TCR 154. TCR 356.

That the Roman Catholics before the Reformation delivered exactly the same things as the Reformed after it, concerning the above-named four articles... with the sole difference that they conjoined the same faith with charity or good works. General article.

That the leading Reformers... retained all the dogmas (named above) such as they then were and had been with the Roman Catholics; but that they separated charity or good works from that faith, and declared them not to be conjointly saving, in order that they might be torn asunder from the Roman Catholics as to the essentials themselves of the Church. General article.
That still the leading Reformers adjoined good works to their faith, and also conjoined them, but in man as a passive subject... General article.
Therefore it may be said to have been provided... that the Reformers cast charity and good works far away from their faith. Explained.
That the Roman Catholics... can be introduced into the New Jerusalem... before the Reformed. General article.
The imputation of the merit of Christ enters like a soul into the universal theology in the Reformed Christian world.
The Reformed have taken contrition in place of repentance, in order to be torn asunder from the Roman Catholics... TCR 516.
As actual repentance... is extremely difficult in the Reformed Christian world... a more easy kind of repentance shall be adduced...
In the Reformed Christian world, by which is meant all those separated from the Roman Catholic Church... actual repentance finds very great resistance. (The reasons ex.)
A Reformed man, so called, is among his like as to his spirit...

I have asked many of the Reformed in the Spiritual World why they have not performed actual repentance, seeing that it has been enjoined on them both in the Word, and also before the Holy Communion. (Their replies.)
As few in the Reformed Christian world perform repentance...
The like loves would burst forth from many of the leaders of the Churches outside Babylon, unless their Power were limited and thus bridled.
As Melancthon had been one of the Reformers of the Church, he was taken out by the Lord's command...
a. The rest of the Christians, who are called the Reformed... when they think of the Lord, think of Him no otherwise than as a common man.
See Last Judgment. SE 5856. LJPost 133. LJPost 178. SE 5649.

The time of the Reformation, when again there was the reading of the Word, and the acknowledgement of the Lord... Signified. But that still interiorly with those who were Reformed there was no truth and good in worship. Signified.
With the Reformed (all the truth of the Church is falsified, and thence all its good. But the converse with the Papists.) AE 949:2.
The Church with the Reformed has been devastated by faith alone; with the Papists by dominion...

From (the Babylonish) thick darkness, the Reformed, who receded from that nation, emerged into some light through the reading of the Word, but not into such light that they could see truths, like the Ancients. The cause was that they separated faith from life; and man has light from life.
It treats here especially of the state of the Church with the Reformed... AE 1021.

Hence it is that of the Divine Providence it took place that some Churches separated themselves from the Babylonish one, which acknowledge the Divine power of the Lord... to be equal to that of God the Father, and also attach Divine holiness to the Word alone. This was provided by the Lord, lest the Christian Church in the European world should utterly fall. Signified.
The truths of the Church from the Word with the Reformed... Signified, Explained.
The Reformed are here meant, who utterly rejected the dogmas which proceeded from the papal consistory. Signified.
This unanimity appears with the Reformed, who are divided into three Churches... but still all three have completely receded from the profane things of Babylon. Signified.
If I had been born at... Rome, and were a Reformed Christian, is my country to be loved for its spiritual good...
The third state of the Christian Church which is called that of the Reformation. Treated of.
